title: FastAPI: routes, Pydantic typing and automatic validation

videos.script: Six lessons of Django. Now the same API again, in FastAPI, in a project of its own beside the first. {{second}} The idea that FastAPI is built on fits in one sentence. The type hints are the specification. A parameter typed as an int is read from the query string and checked. A parameter typed as a model is read from the body and validated. {{types}} The models are Pydantic models. A class whose annotations are the rules. Give it the string fifteen where it wants an integer, and it tells you, field by field. {{pydantic}} Your function never runs with data that failed. When it does run, its arguments are already the right types. {{never}} Then the other direction. A response model says what may leave. The list of who is coming goes out with names and without email addresses, even though the function returned both. {{filter}} And the status codes. 422 when the data does not fit. 404 when the event does not exist. 409 when the data is fine and the world says no.
